en: Kakansan grew wrathful,
uncertainty_note: Какансан is provisionally read as a name or title.

en: We shall bring slaughter upon China.
uncertainty_note: The future verb is clear in sense but its exact handwritten morphology is difficult.

en: Such was the testament that was made,
This is what the ear heard.
Over the eighteen thousand worlds,
There is the Heaven-khan in Beijing.
uncertainty_note: The middle title/name Теңир каны is provisional.

en: Kakansan grew wrathful,
uncertainty_note: Какансан is provisionally read as a name or title.

en: Over the eighteen thousand worlds,
Go and declare your grievance before them.
uncertainty_note: чер is provisionally read as grievance or sorrow.

en: You have many words already spoken,
In Chañu, which was laid waste,
uncertainty_note: Чаңуда is provisionally read as a place name.

en: At the corner where corrupt words were uttered,
uncertainty_note: The final word is provisionally read бурчта.

en: You have a name that can bring ruin.
uncertainty_note: атың may mean name or horse in this context.

en: Over the eighteen thousand worlds,
If you grow wrathful, you will prevail,
uncertainty_note: утарсың is a provisional reading.

en: If you refuse the words that are spoken,
If they will not walk the road appointed,
The great people of Beijing,
When the warrior speaks in anger,
uncertainty_note: The syntax is difficult; Каарданса is provisionally treated as a verb.

en: If you lash the world onward,
Look upon it and act,
uncertainty_note: The phrase карап кылып is provisional.

en: You have put it to the test; know this.
Take the word of Heaven from abroad,
uncertainty_note: Сырттан and тилинди are provisional readings.

en: He gained the land without making a raid,
He took the people who had been overrun,
The nation’s inherited wealth is a tethering stake,
uncertainty_note: казыка is retained as a possible manuscript case form.

en: Heroism requires a people,
To range abroad requires land.
uncertainty_note: Торболоого is a provisional reading.

en: The people are dear, the nation is a pledge,
uncertainty_note: The final word күрөөк is uncertain.

en: What the ear has heard and the eye has seen,
We shall divide it as an inheritance for the people.
uncertainty_note: бөлөрүк is retained as a nonstandard or compressed manuscript form.

en: Kakansan grew wrathful,
uncertainty_note: Какансан is provisionally read as a name or title.

en: All of the wide world,
You will see gathered together.
Saying this, Zhan Zhetpes continued,
uncertainty_note: Жан жетпес is provisionally segmented as a name or epithet.

en: Saying that he had become a sovereign in peace.
uncertainty_note: The opening word is provisionally read Тынып.

en: One from each and every people,
Saying, “Appoint one from among the envoys,”
uncertainty_note: Provisional manuscript reading: ambiguous cursive letterforms or a material variant from the printed continuation; preserve for later collation.

en: Over the eighteen thousand worlds,
Saying, “Let Chyng Temir be the padishah,”
The Kyrgyz of Ala-Too,
Send an envoy between us,
Without clashing or quarreling,
Take counsel and testimony from the people.
uncertainty_note: Provisional manuscript reading: ambiguous cursive letterforms or a material variant from the printed continuation; preserve for later collation.

en: If you clash and quarrel,
Look carefully upon Kenen,
That lion and tiger of a hero,
I examined the valiant man,
Dark outside, blue-gray at heart,
Folding his hands and saying, “Your servant,”
Saying, “We have submitted ourselves to you,”
He is no son who will submit to fortune,
He is no rootless man without a leader,
One accustomed to being driven and handed over,
uncertainty_note: Provisional manuscript reading: ambiguous cursive letterforms or a material variant from the printed continuation; preserve for later collation.

en: These are no Shibe or Torgout people,
His valor is not greater than the people’s,
uncertainty_note: Provisional manuscript reading: ambiguous cursive letterforms or a material variant from the printed continuation; preserve for later collation.

en: Your thunder is not so great,
uncertainty_note: Provisional manuscript reading: ambiguous cursive letterforms or a material variant from the printed continuation; preserve for later collation.

en: The people are not more numerous than the Chinese,
No nation is greater than the white-capped Kyrgyz.
uncertainty_note: Provisional manuscript reading: ambiguous cursive letterforms or a material variant from the printed continuation; preserve for later collation.

en: Do not turn this into a reckless affair,
uncertainty_note: Provisional manuscript reading: ambiguous cursive letterforms or a material variant from the printed continuation; preserve for later collation.

en: Warrior Tengir, heed my words,
What I have said to you is no great thing.
uncertainty_note: Provisional manuscript reading: ambiguous cursive letterforms or a material variant from the printed continuation; preserve for later collation.

en: Bow to one who bows,
He is one of a heroic people,
uncertainty_note: Provisional manuscript reading: ambiguous cursive letterforms or a material variant from the printed continuation; preserve for later collation.

en: They are a people who know cultivation,
uncertainty_note: Provisional manuscript reading: ambiguous cursive letterforms or a material variant from the printed continuation; preserve for later collation.

en: My lord, his road and passage are open,
uncertainty_note: Provisional manuscript reading: ambiguous cursive letterforms or a material variant from the printed continuation; preserve for later collation.

en: He is one of a heroic people.
Broad-jawed and smooth-tongued,
From an eloquent man who never misspeaks,
From one who stands as a shield for the people,
uncertainty_note: Provisional manuscript reading: ambiguous cursive letterforms or a material variant from the printed continuation; preserve for later collation.

en: Whose forefathers were heroes,
One who takes his stand beneath the banner.
uncertainty_note: Provisional manuscript reading: ambiguous cursive letterforms or a material variant from the printed continuation; preserve for later collation.

en: What can excuse the multitude,
uncertainty_note: The opening phrase is a provisional cursive reading; no ordered printed counterpart was found for this line.

en: Who led a people as vast as a multitude,
uncertainty_note: The comparative form Калыңдай is provisional; no ordered printed counterpart was found.

en: Is hardship the fault of the sword,
uncertainty_note: The second half of the line is a difficult cursive reading and remains provisional.

en: From your eye that sees the distant target,
uncertainty_note: The manuscript appears to read Бутадан; the syntax is elliptical and no counterpart was found.

en: From one who foresees the people's fate,
uncertainty_note: The phrase is visually plausible but has no ordered printed counterpart.

en: From one whose speech is wondrous and sweet as sugar,
From one whose skill surpasses the age,
Let us send an envoy between us,
Closing our eyes and saying that God will come,
uncertainty_note: This manuscript-only line replaces material in the printed sequence; кудай келет is provisional.

en: If he should see it by chance,
uncertainty_note: The opening verbal form is a difficult cursive reading and the translation is provisional.

en: If he acts rudely without warning,
The true banner named by Tengir,
uncertainty_note: The final word appears to be туу, but the manuscript syntax is uncertain.

en: Saying he will see it above the house.
uncertainty_note: The line is legible but its relation to the surrounding manuscript-only passage is uncertain.

en: Let us set out far, far away,
uncertainty_note: The repeated adverb and verb are visually plausible but lack a printed counterpart.

en: Let us remain and draw close,
uncertainty_note: The final verb is a provisional cursive reading.

en: Bulls, rams, and camels of every sort,
uncertainty_note: The final compound is difficult cursive and is transcribed provisionally.

en: Let us name the fine ones we behold.
uncertainty_note: Both the opening adjective and middle noun are difficult cursive readings; translation is provisional.

en: Let us test his measure with words,
With wisdom and with speech,
With strategy and skill,
Let us measure him carefully and make him rue it,
uncertainty_note: A manuscript-only variant at this point; the words Чам-чак and муңтайлы are provisional.

en: Let us learn the extent of his powers.
Seeing the raven of power,
uncertainty_note: This line is absent from the printed counterpart; каргын is a provisional cursive reading.

en: Without quarreling or feuding,
Let us mount his throne in triumph.
A swift horse they would not yield if asked,
Let us cast a cold lasso over it.
Their graceful, shimmering girls,
Let us take them as plunder in this way.
So spoke the artful Zhelzhetpes,
uncertainty_note: The printed counterpart reads Деп, ошентип, Желжетпес; өнөрүн is the apparent manuscript variant.

en: Whose cunning no mind could fathom,
A master cultivator of wisdom, the finest,
The finest knower of stratagems,
uncertainty_note: This manuscript line expands the printed sequence; the compound Айла билгич is visually clear but not independently attested here.

en: A clear-eyed sage,
Among the Chinese and the Kyrgyz,
He comes out alone ahead in the contest.
